articles.title: Trump hints at 'big surprises' to come ahead of midterm election
articles.summary: President Donald Trump has already taken several extraordinary actions before the midterms. Now he says more "big surprises" are coming.
articles.body:
WASHINGTON – President Donald Trump teased that he has "big surprises" in store in the weeks before the Nov. 3 midterm election that involve his budget chief, igniting intense speculation among his critics on what the president could be planning.

Trump made the remark on Oct. 6 as he was giving a shoutout to Russell Vought , director of the White House Office of Management and Budget, during a speech near Baltimore on a new Maryland shipyard that will build submarines.

"We have some big surprises coming up in another few weeks, right, Russ?" Trump said. "He's going to be one of the very important people in the history of our country, in my opinion. He's got some great things happening."

The White House did not say when asked what Trump mean by his comments, directing USA TODAY to the OMB, which did not respond to a request for comment.

Trump has already taken several extraordinary actions ahead of the midterms, including spending more than $12 million in government funds to air pro-Trump television ads, issuing $500 Affordable Care Act refund checks to nearly 1 million Americans, and sending $90 apiece to 1 million seniors by diverting funds from a Medicare fund reserved for improvements to the program.

The New York Times reported that Trump personally directed Vought, who served in the same role during Trump's term, to find government money to fund the ad campaign. The money came from $20 million authorized to the Department of Homeland Security . Trump has since promised to use money from his MAGA Inc. Super PAC to pay for the ads, but doesn't plan to reimburse the government for nearly $13 million already spent to air the commercials.

Trump has also pledged to give all adult Americans $5,000 from government revenue if Republicans retain control of the House and Senate ‒ an offer even some MAGA allies have called a bribe for votes.

Vought, one of the president's closest aides, helped write Project 2025, the controversial policy blueprint created by the conservative Heritage Foundation that Trump tried to distance himself from during the 2024 campaign. Vought has taken a leading role in the Trump administration's efforts to slash federal agencies, cut spending and lay off federal workers.

Some Trump critics suggested that the president's hint about "big surprises" could signal efforts to interfere with the election. "Election interference in the offing," Joyce Vance, a former Obama-appointed U.S. attorney for the Northern District of Alabama, said in a post on X .

Trump unsuccessfully tried to overturn his 2020 election loss and still falsely says he won the election.

Leading up to the midterms, the president has regularly accused Democrats of cheating to win elections, without presenting evidence, and tried to sow doubts about the integrity of U.S. elections in a prime-time speech in July. Trump has issued executive orders creating new voting restrictions and directed the Department of Homeland Security to look for noncitizens on the voting rolls.

Trump also led a rare mid-decade redistricting effort in a bid to create more Republican congressional seats before the midterms.

In an interview last week with Time magazine, Trump did not rule out declaring a national emergency around the midterms or invoking the Insurrection Act, which allows the president to deploy the military within the United State during times of civil disorder.

articles.title: Alcolumbre pauta votação da PEC que prevê fim da escala 6x1 para a próxima quarta-feira  | G1
articles.standfirst: Para ser aprovada, uma PEC precisa ter ao menos votos favoráveis de ao menos 49 senadores nas duas votações. Governo articula para concluir votação antes do segundo turno das eleições.
articles.summary: Para ser aprovada, uma PEC precisa ter ao menos votos favoráveis de ao menos 49 senadores nas duas votações. Governo articula para concluir votação antes do segundo turno das eleições.
articles.body:
O presidente do Senado , Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), incluiu na pauta da próxima quarta-feira (14) a votação da proposta de emenda à Constituição (PEC) que prevê o fim da escala 6x1. A pauta prevê a última sessão para discussão da proposta e a votação em primeiro turno do texto no Plenário da Casa.

🔎 Para ser aprovada, uma PEC precisa ter ao menos três quintos dos votos favoráveis nas duas votações. Ou seja, precisa contar com o apoio de 49 senadores .

De acordo com o regimento interno do Senado, a proposta precisa passar por cinco sessões de discussão em plenário antes de ser votada em primeiro turno. Após a primeira votação, é preciso aguardar cinco dias úteis antes da nova análise da proposta.

Após esse período, são necessárias três sessões de discussão. Só depois dessa etapa o texto pode ser submetido à votação em segundo turno.

O regimento, no entanto, prevê a possibilidade de quebra desse período entre os dois turnos de votação para que a análise aconteça de forma mais rápida, a chamada quebra de interstício, mas a maioria simples dos presentes na sessão precisa aprovar.

O governo do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) articula para quebrar prazos e acelerar a votação da medida. A líder do Governo no Senado, Teresa Leitão (PT-PE), está recolhendo assinaturas para pedir calendário especial e votar a proposta antes do segundo turno.

🔎 Segundo o presidente do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), são necessárias 54 assinaturas para votar um requerimento desse tipo, mas já houve momentos em que pedidos com menos apoios foram aceitos pelo plenário do Senado. Também segundo o presidente da Casa, nesses momentos não houve reclamações por parte dos senadores.

Governistas se articulam e dizem já ter os votos necessários para aprovar a proposta.

Já os apoiadores de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) tentam adiar a votação. Na quarta-feira (7), a senadora Tereza Cristina (PP-MS) se reuniu com Alcolumbre para pedir que a votação da PEC fosse realizada somente depois das eleições.

Três das cinco sessões de discussão que precisam ser feitas antes da votação já foram concluídas . As sessões têm sido marcadas pela ausência da maioria dos senadores do PL e da oposição.

Inicialmente, os senadores de oposição buscavam não registrar presença para evitar a discussão, mas senadores governistas e do centro participaram de forma expressiva, chegando a 60 presentes nas sessões, que estão aceitando participação virtual.

A maior parte dos discursos é de apoio ao fim da 6x1. Até o momento, o único senador que apresentou críticas ao texto atual foi Oriovisto Guimarães (PSDB-PR). Ele defende alterações no projeto.

🔎A PEC do fim da jornada 6x1 altera a Constituição para diminuir as horas de trabalho semanais de 44 para 40 horas. Também estabelece que é necessário garantir dois dias de folga remunerada, um deles preferencialmente aos domingos.

A grande mudança é garantir que os trabalhadores tenham dois dias de descanso semanal sem a possibilidade de redução salarial. Preferencialmente, um desses dias deve ser o domingo.

Para que os trabalhadores brasileiros cheguem às 40 horas semanais com dois dias livres haverá um período de transição. Se aprovada, a PEC deve seguir a seguinte cronologia:

em dois meses , redução da jornada semanal para 42 horas , com dois dias de repouso semanal remunerado;

em um ano após esses dois meses , redução da jornada semanal para 40 horas .

A mudança não será aplicada para trabalhadores com ensino superior que ganhem por mês mais de 2,5 vezes o teto do INSS, ou seja, quem ganhe mais de R$ 21.188 por mês.

Presidente do Senado Federal, senador Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP) — Foto: Waldemir Barreto/Agência Senado

articles.title: Datafolha: Eleitores definiram votos para 2026 com antecedência | G1
articles.standfirst: Pesquisa também aponta que, na disputa de 2026, caiu o número de pessoas que deixaram a definição dos seus candidatos para a última hora.
articles.summary: Pesquisa Datafolha revela aumento no número de eleitores que definiram seus candidatos a governador, senador e deputados pelo menos um mês antes do pleito.
articles.body:
Pesquisa Datafolha divulgada nesta sexta-feira (9) aponta que, em comparação com as eleições anteriores, o brasileiro decidiu seu voto para governador, senador e deputados mais cedo em 2026.

A maioria dos eleitores escolheu seus candidatos pelo menos um mês antes do pleito. Para o cargo de governador, o índice subiu de 63% (em 2022) para 69% (em 2026). Com relação aos senadores, aumentou de 50% para 57%. Já para deputados federais, saiu de 50% e para 55%. Por fim, no caso de deputados estaduais, foi de 49% para 55%.

A disputa presidencial teve movimento mais sutil: em 2022, 81% tinham definido seu voto pelo menos um mês antes do pleito; neste ano, o índice chegou a 84%.

A pesquisa também apontou que, em geral, caiu o número de pessoas que deixaram a escolha para a véspera ou para o dia da votação. Em 2022, para os cargos de senador e deputado federal, 25% decidiram de última hora; neste ano, caiu para 20%. Já para governadores, baixou 17% para 14%. Quanto aos deputados estaduais, a queda foi 26% para 21%.

articles.title: PF pede ajuda aos EUA para rastrear verba de filme sobre Bolsonaro | G1
articles.standfirst: Pedido foi encaminhado pela PF ao Ministério da Justiça brasileiro nesta sexta-feira (9). Investigadores querem identificar o destino dos recursos do fundo Havengate.
articles.summary: PF pede ajuda aos EUA para rastrear recursos do fundo Havengate, usado no financiamento do filme Dark Horse sobre o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro.
articles.body:
A Polícia Federal pediu formalmente cooperação aos Estados Unidos para rastrear o destino do dinheiro do fundo Havengate, usado para financiar o filme “Dark Horse”, sobre o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro (PL).

O pedido foi encaminhado pela PF nesta sexta-feira (9) ao Departamento de Recuperação de Ativos e Cooperação Jurídica Internacional (DRCI), do Ministério da Justiça.

A solicitação aos EUA será feita por meio do Tratado de Assistência Jurídica Mútua, conhecido pela sigla em inglês MLAT. O instrumento permite a cooperação e a troca de informações entre os países em investigações e processos criminais.

Os investigadores querem identificar o destino dos recursos do fundo que recebeu dinheiro de Daniel Vorcaro, do Banco Master, para financiar a produção.

Como o g1 já mostrou, Vorcaro chegou a pagar R$ 61 milhões aos produtores do filme por meio do Havengate, nos Estados Unidos. O senador e candidato à Presidência Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) teria negociado com o banqueiro o repasse de US$ 24 milhões — cerca de R$ 134 milhões na época — para financiar a produção.

articles.title: Filhote de anta é resgatado após ser encontrado ferido em canavial  | G1
articles.standfirst: O animal, com cerca de 20 dias de vida, foi resgatado próximo ao Parque Estadual Morro do Diabo, em Teodoro Sampaio (SP). A anta é considerada o maior mamífero terrestre do Brasil.
articles.summary: Um filhote de anta (Tapirus terrestris) foi resgatado após ser encontrado ferido em canavial próximo ao Parque Estadual Morro do Diabo, em Teodoro Sampaio (SP).
articles.body:
Um filhote de anta ( Tapirus terrestris ) foi resgatado após ser encontrado ferido em canavial próximo ao Parque Estadual Morro do Diabo, em Teodoro Sampaio (SP). Ação foi divulgada na sexta-feira (9).

A Fundação Florestal publicou vídeos do resgate e processo de acolhimento ao filhote, que tinha cerca de 20 dias e pesava 13 kg quando foi encontrado, no início de setembro. Assista acima.

Nas imagens, o pequeno animal aparece sozinho em uma área de mata seca, emitindo um som característico da espécie. Em seguida, após o resgate e cuidados veterinários, a anta já é vista em uma jaula, se recuperando.

Filhote de anta é resgatado após ser encontrado ferido em canavial em Teodoro Sampaio (SP) — Foto: Fundação Florestal SP/reprodução

No vídeo, ainda é possível ouvir a voz de uma mulher dizendo ao animal para “mostrar os dentinhos”, o que é feito pela anta. Segundos depois, o filhote aparece dormindo.

Conforme a Fundação Florestal, a anta passou por uma cirurgia para tratar fraturas na tíbia e na fíbula. Ela segue em recuperação e é acompanhada de perto pelas equipes especialistas.

Ainda conforme a entidade, não havia previsão para a Timótea, como foi batizada, voltar à natureza. Ela estásob cuidados da Associação Protetora de Animais Silvestres (APASS), em Assis.

A anta é considerada a “jardineira das florestas” e um dos símbolos do Pontal do Paranapanema, ganhando até filme documentário para ampliar o conhecimento sobre a espécie e reforçar a importância da conservação da fauna brasileira.

A espécie, ameaçada de extinção, é o maior mamífero terrestre da América do Sul . A anta desempenha papel fundamental na regeneração de ecossistemas ao dispersar sementes pelas áreas onde circula.

Ela pode chegar aos 250 quilos e se alimenta principalmente de frutos, desempenhando um papel fundamental na dispersão de sementes, conforme a pesquisadora Patrícia Medici, uma das principais referências mundiais nos estudos sobre a espécie.

Ao se alimentar dos frutos, o animal ingere as sementes junto com a polpa e, após o processo digestivo, elimina esse material pelas fezes, espalhando-o pelas áreas por onde circula, segundo a pesquisadora.

articles.title: Camilo Santana diz que estratégia de campanha é comparar biografias | G1
articles.standfirst: Ex-governador do Ceará e coordenador da campanha também admitiu necessidade do partido reconquistar votos nos estados onde desempenho piorou desde a última eleição presidencial.
articles.summary: Ex-governador do Ceará e coordenador da campanha também admitiu necessidade do partido reconquistar votos nos estados onde desempenho piorou desde a última eleição presidencial.
articles.body:
O senador e coordenador político da campanha de reeleição de Lula (PT), Camilo Santana, disse em entrevista ao GloboNews Mais nesta sexta-feira (9) que a estratégia para recuperar votos na disputa com Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) é "comparar as biografias dos candidatos" e "comparar governos".

"O que representa a biografia do presidente Lula? As pessoas sabem a segurança do seu governo, segurança jurídica, segurança do emprego, segurança da correção com ganho real do salário mínimo, valorização dos professores, o olhar para a saúde para o SUS", declarou.

"Se for comparar com o que foi a insegurança do governo Bolsonaro, que teve a pior taxa de desemprego do país, a falta de investimento. Essa é a realidade que nós queremos mostrar agora nessa campanha, nesse segundo turno." Na avaliação do senador, um governo de Flávio Bolsonaro seria uma continuação do mandato do pai.

Santana citou a sua experiência na época, enquanto governador do Ceará, durante o governo de Jair Bolsonaro. "Eu nunca recebi um pagamento do Ministério da Educação quando fui governador para as obras das escolas. Eu precisei entrar no Supremo Tribunal Federal para pagar os recursos”, disse. "Não tinha a menor relação institucional entre o governo federal e respeito pelos estados brasileiros".

O coordenador da campanha ainda falou sobre a pandemia, o retorno do país ao Mapa da Fome e, segundo ele, o desmonte de políticas sociais do Brasil. "Nós não podemos esquecer isso", afirmou. De acordo com Santana, o primeiro momento do atual mandato de Lula foi a reconstrução de medidas como Farmácia Popular, Mais Médicos e Minha Casa, Minha Vida.

Questionado sobre a piora de desempenho de Lula no Nordeste, o ex-governador do Ceará respondeu que a campanha não tem tempo suficiente para avaliar nos próximos dias se houve algum erro de comunicação ou de estratégia. "O fato é que a gente tem agora que colocar uma meta de recuperar esses votos, né? Não só dos estados do Nordeste, mas também nos estados que o teor diminuiu comparado com 2022. Acho que a única forma que a gente tem de recuperar isso, na minha opinião, é comparando biografias, mostrando quem é Flávio Bolsonaro".

O Nordeste continuou sendo o principal reduto eleitoral de Lula (PT) no primeiro turno de 2026. O presidente foi o candidato mais votado nos nove estados da região, mas terminou a votação com menos votos do que havia recebido quatro anos antes.

Lula somou 21.494.584 votos no Nordeste em 2026. Em 2022, havia recebido 21.753.139. Foram 258.555 votos a menos, uma queda de 1,19%.

Parte expressiva da queda aconteceu no Sudeste, onde Lula perdeu cerca de 1,7 milhão de votos em São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro e Minas Gerais na comparação com o 1º turno da eleição presidencial de 2022. Ao mesmo tempo, Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) obteve 1,3 milhão de votos a mais nesses três estados do que seu pai, Jair Bolsonaro (PL), quatro anos antes.

articles.title: Inquérito das fake news: Fachin nega acesso a Fux e cita arquivo | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidência do STF diz que há 104 procedimentos ligados à investigação em análise; após essa etapa, casos serão encaminhados para manifestação da PGR e posterior arquivamento definitivo.
articles.summary: Fachin analisa 104 procedimentos do inquérito das fake news antes de enviar o caso para manifestação da PGR e posterior arquivamento definitivo no STF.
articles.body:
Ministro Edson Fachin — Foto: Alejandro Zambrana/STF

No despacho, Fachin afirma que ainda há procedimentos que precisam ser analisados antes do processo ser tornado público.

Segundo a Presidência do STF, foram identificados 104 procedimentos ligados ao inquérito, entre petições e investigações preliminares, ainda pendentes de avaliação da Presidência. Depois disso, o inquérito deve seguir para o "arquivamento definitivo" e só então ele será divulgado ( entenda mais abaixo).

Entre os processos que o ministro quer analisar estão os inquéritos das fake news, das milícias digitais, as investigações que levaram às condenações de Bolsonaro e aliados na chamada trama golpista, além da apuração sobre a falsificação de cartões de vacina.

Em resposta, a Presidência do STF informou que três dos quatro procedimentos são públicos e podem ser acessados imediatamente pelo ministro. O acesso ao inquérito das fake news, no entanto, depende da análise dos documentos que ainda estão sob sigilo.

Segundo Fachin, 104 procedimentos ligados ao inquérito, entre petições e investigações preliminares, ainda estão em fase de organização e análise, antes que a Corte defina quais são as medidas que devem ser tomadas em cada caso.

Caberá à PGR avaliar as medidas cabíveis, incluindo eventual apresentação de denúncia ou pedido de arquivamento.

Fachin afirmou que pretende concluir a análise dos procedimentos pendentes e, após o cumprimento das etapas processuais necessárias, promover o arquivamento definitivo do inquérito . É neste momento em que o acesso integral aos documentos será garantido.

Luiz Fux em sessão plenária do STF — Foto: Alejandro Zambrana/STF

A decisão de Fux que pedia o compartilhamento do inquérito foi tomada no âmbito de uma ação do Progressistas (PP), partido que apoia o senador Flávio Bolsonaro na candidatura à Presidência da República, apresentada em abril de 2024, parada desde então.

Esse pedido foi apresentado pelo PP contra decisão do ministro Alexandre de Moraes, relator dos casos, que determinou a apuração separada e sigilosa, por meio de uma petição, dos fatos que levaram à operação Tempus Veritatis.

A operação investigou uma tentativa de golpe por parte da gestão do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro.

O PP argumenta que a decisão de Moraes fere preceitos da Constituição, como a dignidade da pessoa humana, o juiz natural, a segurança jurídica, a vedação a juízo de exceção o devido processo legal e o contraditório.

O partido questiona a definição de Moraes como relator desses casos e cita que, ao longo dos anos, foram tomadas centenas de decisões e despachos sigilosos Fux argumenta que parte do material já está sem sigilo e foi fornecida a advogados.

Segundo o ministro, o acesso é necessário para análise dos pedidos do partido.

"Se a defesa tem acesso aos elementos documentados, a fortiori o tem o ministro desta Corte a quem incumbe decidir sobre a constitucionalidade do procedimento. O Tribunal não pode saber menos do que as partes sobre o que o Tribunal faz", escreveu.

Fux afirmou que não está fazendo nenhuma análise preliminar do caso.

"Nada do que aqui se decide antecipa juízo sobre a validade do ato impugnado, sobre a existência de conexão entre os feitos, sobre a competência desta Corte para as investigações ou sobre o cabimento da arguição. São questões que serão enfrentadas, se for o caso, depois de instruído o feito", disse.

articles.title: Ministério da Justiça pede à PF investigação sobre ameaças contra deputada federal eleita Ana Elisa | G1
articles.standfirst: Pedido foi enviado ao diretor-geral da PF, Andrei Augusto Passos Rodrigues, após a deputada relatar novos ataques nas redes sociais e desativar sua conta no X.
articles.summary: Pedido foi enviado ao diretor-geral da PF, Andrei Augusto Passos Rodrigues, após a deputada relatar novos ataques nas redes sociais e desativar sua conta no X.
articles.body:
O Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública pediu à Polícia Federal nesta sexta-feira (9) a abertura de um inquérito para investigar ameaças de morte e estupro contra a deputada federal eleita por Minas Gerais Ana Elisa Santos Silva (PT).

O pedido foi enviado ao diretor-geral da PF, Andrei Rodrigues, após a deputada relatar novos ataques nas redes sociais e desativar sua conta no X.

No documento, o ministério menciona a afirmação de Ana Elisa Santos Silva de que recebia uma ameaça a cada dois minutos.

A pasta também pediu que a PF adote providências junto ao X e à Meta para fazer cessar as práticas denunciadas e identificar os responsáveis ( leia mais abaixo ) .

Nesta quinta (8), Ana Elisa Santos Silva desativou a conta no X após relatar ameaças de morte e estupro .

Em um vídeo publicado no Instagram, ela afirmou que os ataques haviam se intensificado e chegavam a cada dois minutos.

“Eu acredito que ninguém mereça sofrer ameaça de morte por estar politicamente engajado e tentando defender o que acha melhor para o país”, afirmou a deputada eleita no vídeo.

O ofício do Ministério da Justiça é assinado pela secretária nacional de Acesso à Justiça, Sheila Santana de Carvalho.

Em nota, a secretária afirmou haver “indícios fortes de uma rede para além das fronteiras de Minas Gerais” atuando para silenciar a deputada.

“Violência contra as mulheres não pode jamais ser tolerada. Temos indícios fortes de uma rede para além das fronteiras de Minas Gerais atuando para silenciar a Deputada Ana Elisa. É fundamental uma ação consistente para responsabilização de todos que possam estar atuando para colocar sua vida em perigo”, afirmou.

Ana Elisa Santos Silva já havia denunciado à Polícia Civil ameaças de morte e estupro recebidas durante a campanha eleitoral. A corporação informou ao g1 que a investigação estava em andamento.

Um dos e-mails recebidos pela deputada eleita foi enviado em 5 de setembro. Na ocasião, o autor se identificou como integrante de um grupo supremacista branco, citou dados pessoais de Ana Elisa Santos Silva e também ameaçou familiares dela.

A equipe da deputada informou que providências policiais e judiciais haviam sido adotadas para identificar o responsável pela mensagem.

Ministério cita crime com conteúdo misógino

No pedido à PF, o Ministério da Justiça afirma que crimes cometidos pela internet com conteúdo misógino podem ser investigados na esfera federal.

A pasta diz ainda que, no caso de Ana Elisa Santos Silva, há em tese crime de ameaça contra uma mulher em razão de sua atuação política e pede a investigação e a responsabilização dos autores.

Ana Elisa Santos Silva, de 21 anos, foi eleita deputada federal por Minas Gerais pelo PT.

articles.title: Guilfoyle associate says when she asked him for $100K, it was "quid pro quo"
articles.summary: White House officials were told that text messages between Kimberly Guilfoyle and Eric Deters were real, sources told CBS News.
articles.body:
Businessman Eric Deters said he has "no doubt it was pay to play," claiming Kimberly Guilfoyle, now the U.S. ambassador to Greece and ex-fiancee of Donald Trump Jr., asked him to wire $100,000 to pay her American Express bill in exchange for her help with the Trump administration ahead of Guilfoyle's Senate confirmation hearing.

In an interview with CBS News, Deters said Guilfoyle should "lose her ambassadorship" over her alleged behavior, after texts between the two of them from last July were published in the Wall Street Journal .

"It was quid pro quo," Deters told CBS News White House correspondent Weijia Jiang Thursday.

Deters said he never gave her the money.

"Unfortunately for Kimberly Guilfoyle, at that time, at that moment in time, I didn't have $100,000 to spare to give to Kimberly Guilfoyle, or I actually would have been a dumbass enough to do it."

Deters said he made up an "excuse" that his wife wouldn't go along with it.

White House officials were told that the text messages between Guilfoyle and Deters were authentic, sources familiar with the matter told CBS News. Some Trump aides expressed displeasure about Guilfoyle's actions, they said.

The Wall Street Journal first reported this week that Guilfoyle allegedly reached out to Deters days before her congressional hearing to become a U.S. ambassador, saying she needed $100,000 to pay off her American Express credit debt in a way that wouldn't be publicly visible.

"It won't show up anywhere if you wire money to American Express that's all that will show," Guilfoyle wrote to Deters on July 3, according to screen shots of texts provided to CBS News. "I have been officially announced honey please I need you to get this done for me today," she wrote, punctuating the message with a prayer-hands emoji. Her confirmation hearing took place on July 9.

She sent him "American Express Instructions" in a PDF document.

CBS News has reviewed the texts, which were provided by Deters as part of a 292-page file that included dozens of pages of grievances against Trump world figures, communications with Guilfoyle and others, photos of Deters with Guilfoyle, President Trump, Eric Trump and Trump Jr., and a lengthy excerpt of a book Deters has written.

CBS News has reached out to spokespeople for the State Department and the White House, as well as Guilfoyle.

Deters, a longtime Trump supporter, is a retired lawyer and businessman from Kentucky who was sanctioned by the Ohio Supreme Court in 2021 for engaging in the unauthorized practice of law. He has also run unsuccessfully for Kentucky governor and for Rep. Thomas Massie's U.S. House seat.

For years, Deters has been trying to attract media attention and political support for a push to extradite orthopedic spine surgeon Dr. Abubakar Durrani . The government believes Durrani fled the country while he was awaiting trial for healthcare fraud charges. He was accused of billing Medicare, Medicaid and private insurance companies millions of dollars for unnecessary spinal surgeries that were potentially harmful to patients. Today, Deters said he feels slighted that he never received support for his push to have Durrani extradited to the U.S. from influential Trump world figures.

"I sent Susie Wiles, Don Jr. and Kimberly Guilfoyle an email, and I told them, I said, 'You got until 5 o'clock on Monday to help me out with the Durrani victims,'" he said. "They didn't respond. And I told them, 'If you don't, I'm going to go to the media and try to get the media's help because you're not helping.' So I gave them one last shot, and they ignored me."

In the text messages reviewed by CBS News, Deters, who said he also represents hundreds of Durrani's former patients, may have believed he could benefit from Durrani's extradition to the U.S. He wrote to Trump Jr. and Guilfoyle's podcast producer, Drew Lynch, and suggested, "If anyone in Don Jr or your world has an interest in listening to a pitch on how lots of money could be made for a little money in this Durrani matter let me know."

Deters, who no longer practices law, once stood to gain financially if he were able to successfully sue Durrani.

Just before he took office in 2025 and soon after Guilfoyle and Trump Jr. broke off their engagement, Mr. Trump announced he planned to nominate Guilfoyle to be U.S. ambassador to Greece. But Deters said her influence has waned since her relationship with Trump Jr. ended.

"There was no question that she would do anything for me," Deters said. "The problem was, she was on the outs of the Trump world."

Deters claimed Guilfoyle knew there was something wrong about asking for the payment.

"She knew there was something wrong about it because she kept getting mad at me," Deters said. "I mean, I'm naive, I'm putting stuff in writing, sending it to her. She's getting mad. She wants me to use Signal. I didn't know what Signal was."

In late June 2025, she texted, "Eric, I really wish you would stop papering these things. It's really dangerous and not helpful to you and not helpful to you or me while you could simply just call me on Signal." Deters had just sent her a memo to complain that she had not delivered on things that he had asked of her, including getting him booked on Tucker Carlson's podcast.

"I generously offered you $1 million dollars when Durrani settles if you got me on Tucker," he wrote. He also complained that he had prepared a "concise summary" for then-Attorney General Pam Bondi, but "I have not received nothing concrete."

Deters also sought a meeting with then-IRS Commissioner Billy Long about a tax issue, and he wanted Guilfoyle to send the lyrics to a song he had written to Kid Rock.

Deters said in the memo, "I am not naive or a sucker. I need results. No results. No need for me to pay."

He prodded her over text soon afterward: "As of this moment, I bet there have been no emails AND phone calls by you to Wells [Tucker Carlson's producer], Bondi, Long."

Guilfoyle said his accusation was "completely false" and sent as proof the PDF of a letter in which she congratulated Long on his confirmation and asked him to give his attention to Deters' tax issue.

Deters claimed he has paid Guilfoyle and members of the Trump family in the past.

"I paid her a total of $300,000," he said. "Don, Jr. $200,000 for two appearances. Eric Trump for $100,000, $125,000 for President Trump's PAC, $100,000 to go to Kentucky Derby with Trump. So, I paid a lot of money to Trump World," he said, adding that he never owed money to Guilfoyle or anyone else around Mr. Trump.

According to the documents he shared with CBS News, he says he paid Guilfoyle a total of $300,000 for appearance fees. And he said his promise of further payments to Guilfoyle and Lynch was to be for their services as consultants.

The Trump administration's response so far

In Greece, where Guilfoyle greeted his plane earlier this week, Secretary of State Marco Rubio chastised reporters for asking about the matter.

"You guys walk around thinking that because some source told you something and you reported it, it's the gospel," he said. "It's not the gospel. It's not the gospel for me. That's not the way we do things."

Rubio also declined to comment because the story had only "literally posted a few hours ago," telling reporters that "we don't conduct these things in a press conference, on a tarmac, in a foreign country." As Rubio departed Greece, Guilfoyle was present, but off to the side .

CBS News on Thursday asked Vice President JD Vance about the propriety of a government official asking someone to pay off their debt.

CBS News senior White House reporter Jennifer Jacobs asked: "Do you have any reaction to a U.S. government official, in this case a U.S. ambassador, asking someone to pay off debt in exchange to access to other government officials?"

"With that hypothetical, obviously I don't love that, but I, you know, I don't know exactly who you're talking about. I don't know the full details," Vance responded.

Deters insisted his relationship with Guilfoyle was purely political.

"Kimberly Guilfoyle and I have absolutely zero personal relationship, nada," he told CBS News.

But Deters is now determined to share his story. He said he wants to draw attention to Dr. Durrani's victims. And he wants Guilfoyle out of her post as U.S. ambassador.

"I'm a tough hombre," Deters said. "I'm going to get to take Kimberly Guilfoyle's deposition."

articles.title: Hegseth faces bipartisan backlash over public execution for Fort Hood shooter
articles.summary: Both Republican and Democratic critics said the plan was beneath the United States.
articles.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's surprise plan to livestream the military's first execution in six decades drew fierce blowback from both sides of the aisle.

Senior lawmakers from both parties said the plan to broadcast the scheduled Dec. 3 firing squad execution of former Army Maj. Nidal Malik Hasan amounted to a dishonorable public spectacle that could inspire terrorism.

Hasan was court-martialed for the killing of 13 people in a 2009 shooting at Fort Hood, Texas, and sentenced to death. And while many Republicans back the death penalty for Hasan, even some staunch conservatives blanched at the notion of allowing the public to watch it carried out.

"I absolutely support the sentence of death, but live-streaming executions is what jihadists do," Rep. Austin Scott (R-Ga.), a senior member of the House Armed Services Committee, said in a social media post . "America is better than that."

Republican Sen. John Curtis of Utah urged Hegseth to "reconsider" the decision.

"A civilization erodes when it cultivates an appetite for executions as a form of entertainment," Curtis said on X . "Secretary Hegseth's plan to livestream the Fort Hood execution risks feeding that appetite."

Sen. Thom Tillis (R-N.C.), one of the most vocal GOP critics of Hegseth's management of the Pentagon, similarly ripped the effort as "beyond disgusting" on Thursday. "Public executions are what oppressive dictatorships like Iran and Afghanistan do. It should not be happening in America," he said.

A former senior Trump administration official also criticized the move. Joe Kent, who led the National Counterterrorism Center before resigning in March in protest over the Iran war, criticized the tactic as "beneath the dignity" of the country.

"Streaming his execution is not just a stain on our morality — it also gives the terrorists free propaganda that they will use to radicalize & recruit more terrorists like Hassan [sic]," Kent said on X .

President Donald Trump earlier this week approved moving ahead with a firing squad to execute Hasan. Hegseth declared Thursday in an interview that the execution would take place at Fort Hood and that the Pentagon would "make sure that people are able to watch it, that it's public."

Rep. Adam Smith (D-Wash.), the top Democrat on the House Armed Services Committee, said a public execution "makes a mockery of our legal system."

"There is a reason why we treat the meting out of justice with the seriousness it demands," Smith said in a statement. "We are a democratic country and should take the rule of law seriously, not turn it into a spectacle."

The move is without modern precedent in the U.S., and it also raised questions over whether social media platforms would carry to the livestream. American platforms explicitly bar the livestreaming of executions.

The military has not carried out an execution since 1961, when Army Pvt. John Bennett was hanged in front a small audience for rape and attempted murder. And the U.S. has not held a public execution since at least 1936.

Hegseth acknowledged that similar plans for a public military execution haven't been made since around World War II. But the Pentagon chief argued, "I kind of like the mentality we had in WWII — which was win, understand that when the enemy attacks you, you stand your ground."

Sen. Patty Murray (D-Wash.) called for the Pentagon to rescind the plans immediately.

"We can seek justice in this country without glorifying violence and turning an execution into a grotesque public spectacle," she said on X . "What this criminal did was abhorrent and must be punished — but we as a country cannot condone livestreaming a man's death for entertainment."

Sen. Ruben Gallego (D-Ariz.) added that "the U.S. government and victims can have justice without us creating a snuff film."

Not all lawmakers objected to the plan for a public execution.

Rep. Andy Ogles (R-Tenn.) said on X that "public execution is what this terrorist deserves" and called the decision to broadcast the event "excellent."

The case could still be hung up for years depending on possible appeals, retired Air Force lawyer Lt. Col. Rachel VanLandingham said. Hasan could still file a habeas corpus relief in federal court, or his legal team or another party could file a motion to appeal the sentence.

Hasan represented himself during his 2013 court martial, though a civilian legal team has remained involved with his case. If his lawyers or Hasan himself appeals, the execution could be delayed for "years" as the case works its way through the court system, VanLandingham said.

The former commander of Fort Hood, retired Lt. Gen. Sean MacFarland, wrote on social media Thursday that while as commander of the base he approved the death sentence, "it is fair to ask whether carrying out the sentence at Fort Hood and live streaming it is justice, vengeance, or a mere spectacle for the masses."

Livestreaming the execution of the wheelchair-bound Hasan "surrenders a piece of the moral high ground we have held up to now in our campaigns against Al Qaeda and ISIS by adopting their barbaric practice of video recording the executions of their prisoners," MacFarland wrote.

Paul McLeary contributed to this report.
authors: Connor O'Brien, Mark Satter and Leo Shane III

This year’s Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to Navi Pillay , a leading figure in international human rights law, coming as Israel and the U.S. seek to tear down the institutions she has helped build up.

“At a time of existential challenges – including more wars and conflicts than the world has seen in a long time – international law is no longer just a supplement to peace and security. It is an absolute necessity,” the committee wrote in its announcement.

“And yet, the system of international law is under tremendous pressure, and its institutions are under attack. We see a shift towards power politics at the expense of legal frameworks and global respect for law and justice.”

Pillay’s resume: The jurist previously served as the United Nations human rights chief and was a judge at the International Criminal Court (ICC).

As a judge at the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, she helped establish that sexual violence and propaganda could constitute genocide.

She is currently an ad hoc judge at the International Court of Justice, in a case alleging that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya ethnic minority.

Perhaps most controversially, Pillay led a U.N. commission that found last year that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza.

Angry reactions: Israel’s government fumed over the choice.

“If there were an award for lies, hatred, and blood libels, Navi Pillay wouldn’t just be a contender. She’d be a frontrunner. Her role in the relentless, politically motivated demonization of Israel and promotion of the genoLIE speaks volumes,” Israel’s Foreign Ministry wrote in a post on the social platform X .

President Trump shared a post from attorney David Schoen , who worked on his second impeachment trial.

“Today the Nobel Committee shamed itself beyond repair and demeaned the once great Nobel Peace Prize by giving it to the UN’s Navi Pillay. Pillay is an unabashed hater of America and Israel,” Schoen wrote in a post on Truth Social .

Timely move: Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced Friday that the U.S. is imposing full blocking sanctions against the ICC, escalating its fight against the global judicial body.

“We will ban transactions with this rogue court, cutting off their resources and crippling their ability to operate against us,” Rubio said in a video message.

Pillay had Trump on her mind shortly after learning she won the prize.

“If you clap a little bit more, I may share this prize with Trump,” Pillay said in a video clip shared from the moment she heard the news in Nuremberg, Germany.

Last year’s prize winner, Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado , presented her award to Trump in Washington after the president openly coveted the honor.

Trump’s team did not make a public push for the prize this year.

Collins condemned racism and antisemitism but hit back by calling Ossoff a “trust fund kid” who can’t relate to Georgians struggling with high prices.

“No, you owe me an apology,” Jackson shot back.

And he’s not alone. Sen. Chris Murphy (D-Conn.) called the idea “medieval,” asking whether the Pentagon chief was trying to mimic ISIS executions.

articles.title: When ICE hides detainees, constitutional rights go missing
articles.summary: ICE is making thousands of detainees “disappear.” That’s not just cruel — it’s illegal.
articles.body:
Thousands of people in ICE custody have been effectively “disappeared” by the U.S. government, according to new reporting by The Associated Press .

The names of immigrant detainees with final orders of removal have vanished from the Online Detainee Locator System , a database that lets families and lawyers find out where detainees are.

Nearly 16,000 people booked into ICE detention in July were subject to final removal, the AP noted — more than one-third of the overall bookings.

This policy of hiding the location of some detainees reflects the cruel and secretive nature of the administration’s immigration crackdown. It raises serious logistical and legal issues, and should be recognized for what it is: an assault on due process and constitutional rights.

To be clear, this move does not apply to all detainees — just those with a final order of removal. A final order of removal is a document issued by an immigration judge that directs a non-citizen to leave the U.S.

However, persons with final orders of removal may still have options to re-open their cases or file appeals. Some people with final orders are eligible for humanitarian relief under the United Nations Convention Against Torture, which prohibits sending people back to countries where they would face persecution or torture. Many people are issued final orders because they unintentionally missed a court date , or because a government notice was sent to the wrong address .

That’s why the locator system is important. The system is a lifeline for detainees, their families, and their legal counsel. Families use the system to get in touch with their loved ones; immigration attorneys use it to set up meetings with their clients and gather evidence for cases.

As if it were not enough to wipe people’s names from the online locator, the Washington Post reports that immigration officials are now barred from revealing the locations of detainees to their relatives or attorneys over the phone. This puts the burden of communication on detainees. Yet it is not easy for people in detention to make phone calls to the outside. Calls are expensive , and often involve long lines and facility restrictions.

It is especially paramount that detainees are able to make contact, as ICE is constantly transfers people all around the country and even is carrying out illegal deportations .

Removing people from the online locator system itself is likely illegal. Obstructing detainees from access to legal counsel violates their due process rights under the Fifth Amendment, because a lawyer cannot adequately represent their client if they don’t know where they are. Most critically, the move interferes with habeas corpus, a legal process that allows all people to challenge their detention in court. This mechanism is enshrined in the Constitution — and it is available to both citizens and non-citizens.

Legal arguments aside, what reasonable person believes that government-enforced disappearances of prisoners is a good idea? This is a concept associated with authoritarian regimes like North Korea and the former Soviet Union. For Americans who worry about “the deep state,” this policy seems like a good example of it in action.

In a statement , ICE said that detainees with final removal orders were being prioritized for deportation, even though ICE faces a “historic number of injunctions” from courts stopping individual removals. This answer is telling. As of May, federal judges have indeed ruled against the Trump administration in more than 20,000 ICE cases. But if the agency is facing so many court decisions blocking its actions, the solution is not to make detainees harder to trace. The solution is for ICE to reform its practices so that they comply with the law.

Meanwhile, the stakes for people in immigration detention could not be higher. This year is on track for a record number of detainee deaths, and the administration has been sending detainees to remote third-world countries like Eswatini and Rwanda . The inability of a lawyer to reach a client in detention could have life-altering consequences.

If pollsters are correct and Democrats regain control of Congress in the November midterms, lawmakers must ensure that the names of all immigrant detainees appear correctly in the online locator system. Lawmakers could also require that the locator stay updated in a timely manner and that lawyers be notified of detainee transfers. Government-sanctioned disappearances do not belong in a democracy.

Raul A. Reyes is an immigration attorney and television commentator in New York City.

articles.body:
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin bashed New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) on Friday for his response to a recent Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) involved shooting in the city.

Mullin said Mamdani’s public statements are dangerous and that he is performing “political theater.”

“I am speaking facts; the mayor speaks with political tone,” Mullin said at a press conference Friday. “His words are dangerous and incite hostility; it doesn’t help.”

An ICE officer shot an immigrant — later identified as Oscar Belgal, a 28-year-old from the Dominican Republic — in the neck Thursday while he was driving with a 5-year-old child in the car. Belgal, who has a criminal record, was taken to an area hospital, and the child remains unharmed and with a family member.

Mamdani railed against ICE at a press conference Thursday night and said there was no explanation for the tactics used. The mayor said he spoke with President Trump and Mullin Thursday night in an attempt to get Belgal released but was unsuccessful.

Mullin said Trump agreed to release Belgal to New York Police Department (NYPD) custody if it was willing to pursue charges against him, but he said Mamdani did not agree. He said Belgal may have been in the U.S. for the past three years, during which he participated in “extensive criminal activity.”

Mamdani called for ICE to release body-camera footage of the incident. The NYPD on Friday released body-camera footage from its officers of the moments after the shooting .

Mullin went after the mayor for calling Belgal a New Yorker and criticized Mamdani’s statement that “ICE is rotten to the core.” Mamdani has called for the abolishment of ICE.

“Really? The men and women of ICE each day are enforcing the laws that he refuses to enforce,” Mullin said. “We arrest thousands weekly that are criminals, going after the worst of the worst, and he turns a blind eye to it.”

Mullin said ICE was serving a lawful order and that Belgal had evaded officers once before. He said ICE was not aware that the child was in the car during the encounter and that the officers involved will be put on administrative leave while it investigates the situation.

The secretary said Belgal did know the child was there when he accelerated his car to a “high speed” and that the public should blame him.

“The public outcry should be also toward this criminal, this thug, this gang-banger, this possible murderer,” Mullin said.

NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch said Belgal pleaded guilty to grand larceny and that an investigation into the criminal sale of drugs involving Belgal is ongoing and had been taken over by federal agents.

articles.title: Collins touts early release of home heating assistance money
articles.summary: Sen. Susan Collins (R-Maine), who is facing a tough reelection fight, on Friday touted the early release of funds to help low-income people heat their homes. “After my conversations with the HHS [Health and Human Services] Secretary and OMB [Office of Management and Budget] Director this week, more than $38 million in federal home heating…
articles.body:
Sen. Susan Collins (R-Maine), who is facing a tough reelection fight, on Friday touted the early release of funds to help low-income people heat their homes.

“After my conversations with the HHS [Health and Human Services] Secretary and OMB [Office of Management and Budget] Director this week, more than $38 million in federal home heating assistance will be released to help Maine families,” Collins said on the social platform X .

“This is one of the earliest releases of LIHEAP funding. This announcement comes at a critical time, as rising home heating oil prices are placing significant financial pressure on Mainers,” she added, referring to the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program.

Collins’s announcement comes as fuel prices, including heating oil , which is commonly used in the Northeast, have spiked amid the U.S.-Iran war and Ukraine’s attacks on Russian oil refineries.

The high prices have put pressure on Americans’ wallets — and on candidates seeking reelection.

In a recent debate , Collins’s Democratic opponent, Troy Jackson, called for more LIHEAP money, expanding eligibility and ending the war in Iran.

Collins during the debate mentioned her talks with the Trump administration to ask for early relief and called for expanding the program and expanding programs to help people weatherize their homes.

While LIHEAP has significant bipartisan support in Congress, the Trump administration has been critical of the program, repeatedly proposing to defund it in budget requests to Congress. The administration also fired staffers working on the program last year.

In an email to The Hill, Mark Wolfe, executive director of the National Energy Assistance Directors Association, which represents state-level LIHEAP directors, praised the decision as a meaningful step. He said he hopes Congress will also devote more money to the program.

“This is record time. Usually we don’t see the money for 30 days. This will definitely help cold weather states get their programs started early … and provide immediate relief to families using heating oil,” Wolfe said in an email.

“Hopefully it’s the first step in addressing the need for additional money…as prices for heating oil continue to hit record levels,” he added.

Collins is the chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, whose bills dictate federal spending.

articles.title: Dem scrambles to change tune on trans athletes as Trump targets past record: ‘Annie Trannie’
articles.summary: South Carolina U.S. Senate candidate Annie Andrews claims she was misrepresented on transgender sports after Trump dubbed her "Annie Trannie."
articles.body: A South Carolina Democrat running for U.S. Senate who previously opposed legislation restricting transgender athletes' participation in girls' sports is now emphasizing her opposition to biological males participating in female athletics as President Donald Trump targets her record ahead of the midterm elections. Trump took aim at Annie Andrews, a pediatrician challenging Republican Sen. Darline Graham, in a series of Truth Social posts this week, dubbing her "Annie Trannie" and accusing her of supporting transgender policies that are out of step with South Carolina voters. The president also shared an attack ad accusing Andrews of supporting biological males competing against female athletes. "Annie Andrews is for they/them, not for our values, not for South Carolina," the ad said. But Andrews pushed back in an interview with Fox News Digital on Thursday, arguing that her positions have been misrepresented. "I don't support biological men playing in women's sports and I don't support gender surgery on minors," Andrews said. Her comments stand in contrast to her public opposition to South Carolina's 2022 Save Women’s Sports Act, which restricted transgender athletes' participation in girls' and women's school sports. At the time, Andrews called the legislation "shameful" and "actively harmful," raising questions about how she reconciles her past opposition to the law with her current campaign position. DEMOCRATS ARE CHANGING THEIR TRANSGENDER MESSAGE. REPUBLICANS SAY THEY’RE JUST FLIP-FLOPPING As passed, the bill required interscholastic, intercollegiate, intramural and club teams sponsored by public schools and colleges to be designated as male or female-coded. It then closed women’s teams to male students and similarly closed men’s sports to women — unless the school did not have a designated women’s team. Private schools competing against public schools were required to follow the same rules. It also allowed students harmed by a violation to sue schools. Andrews’ social media post at the time garnered resurfaced attention as she launched her 2026 Senate bid, attracting pressure from Republicans. "Annie "Trannie" Andrews is running against our wonderful Darline Graham for the Senate in South Carolina," Trump wrote in one post. "Annie Trannie is not, in particular, as it pertains to representing the Values of the Great People of South Carolina — She is in favor of Transgender for Everyone, Open Borders, Defunding the Police, High Taxes, a Weak Military, and will absolutely fight to take your guns away — In other words, she is against our Great Second Amendment! Trannie is not for South Carolina, and South Carolina must show, in the upcoming Election, that it is not for her," Trump added. In her interview with Fox News Digital, Andrews dismissed Trump's barb, calling it a distraction from the issues central to voters in South Carolina. "And in regards to the name-calling, if calling me names is going to lower gas and diesel prices here for so many hardworking South Carolinian families, if it’s going to lower grocery prices or somehow make healthcare more affordable then he can call me all the names he wants but I don’t think that’s a path to solution so I’m going to stay focused on what I can do to help folks in South Carolina," Andrews said. Andrews did not immediately respond to additional requests for comment on whether her statements reflected a change in stance. She also did not expand on what had drawn criticism for the Save Women’s Sports Act. TALARICO CAMP SAYS HE OPPOSES TRANS ATHLETES IF UNSAFE OR UNFAIR BUT ACCUSES POLITICIANS OF BULLYING STUDENTS At least one Republican onlooker, National Republican Senatorial Regional Press Secretary Nick Puglia, believes her remarks speaks poorly of the message she's presenting to voters. "Annie Andrews' blatant lies show just how desperate she is and how little she thinks of South Carolinians. But nothing Andrews says or does will change her far-left record," Puglia said in a comment. This isn't the first time Andrews has received Republican criticisms for what they view as retreats from trans policies. In 2022, Rep. Nancy Mace, R-S.C., called out Andrews for, in her view, trying to walk back her opposition to H. 4047, a bill that would "prohibit the performance of a medical procedure or the prescription or issuance of medication, upon or to a minor, that is intended to alter the appearance of the minor's gender or delay puberty, with exceptions; to create criminal penalties; and for other purposes." Andrews said she opposed the bill in a post to X, calling it "dangerous," only to later say that she opposed trans procedures for minors. "She called the legislation to ban that kind of surgery dangerous. She called that legislation an attack on our youth. And it wasn't until we called her out on it that she decided that she's now not for something that she was very publicly in support of just last year. And so it's really hard to play hide and seek from your public comments, because once you tweet it, it's on their public record forever. And that's how we discovered it," Mace told Fox News Digital at the time. Notably, she isn’t the only Democrat who in recent weeks has received attention for seeming shifts in her position over transgender policies. Fellow Democrats like Rep. Marcy Kaptur, D-Ohio, Rep. Don Davis, D-N.C., and Sarah Trone Garriott, a congressional candidate in Iowa, have all been forced to reiterate their positions as Republicans have highlighted their records on the subject. WATCH: BATTLEGROUND DEMOCRAT CALLED IOWA A 'BACKWATER' OVER TRANSGENDER ATHLETES BAN In Kaptur’s case, she described how she had "voted with Republicans to keep transgender ideology out of our schools" despite voting against a women’s sports bill. Similarly, Davis voted "present" on that same women’s bill while later claiming that women should have "safe and fair space" in sports. And Garriott, who cast a vote against a ban on biological men in women’s locker rooms, clarified her stance earlier this year, stating that "I oppose letting men in women’s locker rooms." Those statements reflect broader trends in public opinion showing consensus on trans athlete policies. Recently, the Pew Research Center found in a Aug. 11 report that 73% of respondents were "not at all" or "not too" comfortable with "athletes competing on sports teams that do not match their sex at birth," compared to just 13% that replied that they were "extremely" or "very" comfortable with the idea. Similarly, 66% of participants said they would support laws or policies requiring trans athletes to compete on teams that match their biological sex compared to 15% who said they would oppose such policies. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP With just four weeks left to address criticisms over her views, Andrews now heads to South Carolina’s general election on Nov. 3., having cleared the state's Democratic primary earlier this year in June.

articles.title: Marco Rubio announces sweeping financial sanctions against the International Criminal Court
articles.summary: Marco Rubio announced the Trump administration will soon freeze ICC assets and bar all U.S. transactions with the International Criminal Court.
articles.body: Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced Friday that the Trump administration is imposing sweeping financial sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC), a body the president has sought to dismantle throughout his second term. To date, the administration has sanctioned 17 individuals with ties to the ICC, including judges and prosecutors. The latest move marks the first time the U.S. has gone after the institution itself. "Our message is clear: The United States and the American people are not subject to the jurisdiction of this fake ICC," Rubio said in a pre-recorded video message released Friday morning. "Both parties agree on this, but only President Trump has the resolve to take the action needed to end this threat once and for all." This comes hours after this year's Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to Navanethem "Navi" Pillay, a former ICC judge. TRUMP ADMINISTRATION SANCTIONS SITTING PRESIDENT OF THE INTERNATIONAL CRIMINAL COURT FOR 'ABUSES OF POWER' In a statement Friday, the Netherlands-based court strongly condemned the U.S. sanctions as "an assault on the rule of law and on the very foundations of the international legal order." "This measure targets an independent judicial institution, created by treaty and entrusted by 125 States Parties with investigating and prosecuting genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes and the crime of aggression," the ICC added. "It is an attempt to obstruct the course of justice and to prevent the Court from doing what it was created to do." ICC President Tomoko Akane, who was personally sanctioned by the Trump administration in August, said the court will continue to operate despite the new penalties. In announcing the sanctions, Rubio argued the ICC believes it has the authority to prosecute American service members operating overseas and even U.S. Border Patrol agents. There is no evidence the court has sought to investigate or prosecute Border Patrol agents, though Rubio previously raised that possibility in July. WORLD COURT PROSECUTOR WHO WENT AFTER NETANYAHU FOR WAR CRIMES SUSPENDED OVER SEXUAL MISCONDUCT The administration's concerns about U.S. personnel are not entirely hypothetical. In 2017, an ICC prosecutor sought authorization to investigate alleged war crimes committed by U.S. military and intelligence personnel in Afghanistan. ICC judges initially rejected the request, but that decision was overturned on appeal in 2020, allowing the investigation to proceed. The court's prosecutor later de-prioritized alleged crimes involving U.S. personnel to focus on alleged crimes committed by the Taliban and ISIS-K. Under the new sanctions, any ICC assets subject to U.S. jurisdiction will be frozen, while Americans, U.S. businesses and banks are generally barred from conducting transactions with the court. The sanctions will not go into effect immediately. The Treasury Department has given the ICC a 180-day general license to maintain its operations, giving the court time to address U.S. concerns. ICC TURNS 'BLIND EYE' TO TOP WORLD THREATS WHILE TARGETING AMERICANS, TRUMP ADMIN SAYS "Either the ICC will end its threats, or we will end the ICC. And we expect our allies, many of whom are part of the ICC and that rely on American service members for their defense, to rein in this rogue court," Rubio said. "If they do not, the United States will continue its campaign to dismantle the ICC piece by piece until Americans are threatened no longer." One of the other major grievances the administration has with the ICC is its decision to issue arrest warrants for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former Defense Minister Yoav Gallant in 2024. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The ICC argued both officials were responsible for war crimes and crimes against humanity against Palestinians in Gaza during Israel's military response to the Hamas-led Oct. 7 terrorist attacks in 2023. Both men have denied wrongdoing. In a February 2025 executive order authorizing sanctions against ICC officials, President Donald Trump called the arrest warrants "baseless" and said the court overstepped its authority since Israel was not an ICC member. The ICC maintains that it can exercise jurisdiction over nationals of non-member states when they are accused of qualifying crimes committed on the territory of a state that has accepted the court’s jurisdiction.

articles.title: Trump names Leavitt successor after weeks of speculation — and she's no stranger to MAGA
articles.summary: Katie Zacharia has been offered a job as the next White House Press Secretary
articles.body: President Donald Trump tapped a trusted ally from the company behind his Truth Social platform to become his next White House press secretary Friday, naming attorney and television commentator Katie Zacharia to succeed Karoline Leavitt. Two White House officials confirmed the selection to Fox News Digital before Trump publicly announced the appointment on X. Zacharia, an attorney and frequent television commentator, currently serves as senior communications adviser to Trump Media & Technology Group, which operates the president's social media platform, Truth Social. She will succeed former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt. "It is my Great Honor to have just appointed, as Press Secretary, Katie Zacharia. Katie currently serves as Senior Communications Advisor to Truth Social (Trump Media & Technology Group), where she has been outstanding!" Trump wrote Friday afternoon. KAROLINE LEAVITT JOINS FOX NEWS AS CONTRIBUTOR AFTER LEAVING WHITE HOUSE PRESS SECRETARY ROLE Zacharia celebrated the appointment in a post on X, thanking Trump for what she called the "distinguished privilege" of serving as White House press secretary. "Serving President Trump and the American people at this critical 250-year mark is the honor of a lifetime," Zacharia wrote. "President Trump has shown America that we can be great again, and he works to effectuate that greatness every single day. His confidence is a true privilege, and his leadership is a blessing to this country." Zacharia said her focus would be on communicating the administration's accomplishments to the American public while working with reporters across the country. "The work ahead is to continue delivering strong results for our Country and communicating to the American people the major wins that this Administration is making every single day," she wrote. "I look forward to working with the White House press corps, and with reporters across the country, to get that record out." She also acknowledged the expectations that come with succeeding Leavitt. "Following the fabulous Karoline Leavitt is a high standard, and one worth meeting," Zacharia wrote. Zacharia previously served briefly as a spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security following the departure of Tricia McLaughlin, who had served as press secretary under former DHS Secretary Kristi Noem. KAROLINE LEAVITT HEADS FOR WHITE HOUSE EXIT AS SPECULATION BUILDS OVER WHO TRUMP PICKS NEXT "Katie is a distinguished Graduate of Pepperdine University, and the Pepperdine Caruso School of Law, an attorney, and a frequent Commentator on outlets, including Fox News and Newsmax. She was previously involved in my Campaigns, assisting in key Swing States, where we won 7 out of 7. She has an unblemished record of support, and has been a loyal and brilliant supporter, right from the beginning," said Trump. "She is, likewise, a devoted fan and member of MAGA! I am confident that Katie will deliver strong results for our Country as the next White House Press Secretary, as she has the respect of, and will work fantastically with, the Media, the American People, and my Administration. Katie is replacing the fabulous Karoline Leavitt, who did a fantastic job as Press Secretary. Good luck Katie," he added. A 41-year-old mother of four, Zacharia has been married to her husband Tyler since 2011. He is a producer known for projects like the 2019 film "The Irishman" and 2025 movie, "Roofman." Zacharia notes on her Instagram that her husband has also worked with Angel Studios on "David," "Brink of War" and "Young Washington." WHITE HOUSE PLANS GUEST HOSTS FOR PRESS BRIEFINGS WHILE KAROLINE LEAVITT TAKES MATERNITY LEAVE Since Leavitt's departure, there have been only two formal White House press briefings — one with Vice President JD Vance and one with Attorney General Todd Blanche. The White House adopted a rotating lineup of top Trump administration officials to lead press briefings while former press secretary Karoline Leavitt was on maternity leave over the summer. "Katie has been an effective champion of MAGA movement and America First policies - and most importantly clearly has [the] trust of President Trump," former Trump press secretary Sean Spicer told Fox News Digital. "Anyone who has not met her yet will quickly see that she is a genuinely kind person who will work well with the press corps, unlike the first press secretary who came across as an angry leprechaun at times," Spicer added. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Secretary of State Marco Rubio kicked off the rotation, followed by Vice President JD Vance, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz. Rather than relying on a single deputy press secretary, the administration tapped high-profile officials to field questions from reporters on the president’s agenda. Names previously floated as potential replacements for Leavitt included former Trump attorney and current Justice Department adviser Alina Habba, CNN political commentator Scott Jennings, principal deputy White House press secretary Anna Kelly, White House deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller, former Pence communications director Katie Miller, White House communications director Steven Cheung and Breitbart Washington bureau chief Matthew Boyle.

articles.title: El rey Mohamed VI de Marruecos rompe su silencio sobre la crisis migratoria en Ceuta y envía un mensaje a España: "Ni presiones, amenazas ni chantajes"

articles.summary: El monarca marroquí se pronunció en el discurso de apertura de la nueva legislatura parlamentaria de su país
articles.body: Han pasado ya más de dos meses de la llegada masiva de cientos de migrantes procedentes de Marruecos de manera ilegal a Ceuta. La situación dejó varios muertos y cientos de miles de ellos acampados y presentes en la ciudad autónoma ceutí, algo que sigue siendo habitual a día de hoy. Los vecinos denuncian inseguridad al respecto y que la situación es insostenible. Las reacciones sobre el asunto continúan llegando, siendo la primera vez que se manifiesta sobre ello el rey Mohamed VI de Marruecos este viernes, 9 de octubre. Lo hizo en un discurso en la apertura de la nueva legislatura parlamentaria de su país. Mohamed VI comenzó su intervención de manera tajante, pero sin mencionar expresamente a nadie en concreto: “Declaraciones irresponsables de círculos políticos y mediáticos en España. La relación con España es una elección soberana y no puede supeditarse a ningún tipo de presiones, amenazas ni chantajes” Además, el rey de Marruecos fue más allá sobre la relación con nuestro país: “Ha registrado importantes avances en distintos sectores, incluido el de la lucha contra la inmigración irregular". No obstante, el monarca marroquí insistió acerca de la inmigración irregular: “Se enfrenta a importantes desafíos, vinculados a ciertas disposiciones legales anticuadas y decisiones judiciales alejadas de la realidad". En este sentido, criticó el retraso en la repatriación de menores: “Este comportamiento dificulta la repatriación de menores y de las personas que usurpan el estatus de refugiados, y agudiza el apetito de las redes criminales". “El modelo actual de cooperación ha alcanzado sus límites, como atestiguan claramente las crisis recurrentes”, sentenció. Por último, Mohamed VI anunció que su país propondrá a sus socios “una nueva estrategia” para impulsar el “desarrollo común” y la “estabilidad regional”.

articles.title: Trump strikes deal with Putin to get diesel in sharp reversal of US policy weeks before midterms
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump said he has struck a deal to obtain diesel from Russia, a stunning reversal of years of U. pressure on Moscow over i...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump said he has struck a deal to obtain diesel from Russia, a stunning reversal of years of U.S. pressure on Moscow over its war with Ukraine and an attempt to address high fuel prices ahead of the U.S. midterm elections.

Trump said on social media on Friday that he struck the deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin in a phone call in which he was expected to discuss a suspected case of plague in Russia. Instead, Trump announced that Russia will immediately supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel, followed by an additional 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons "immediately thereafter." Russia will deliver an additional 3 million tons "within a short period of time" after that, he wrote.

Trump's shocking announcement comes after he signed a sweeping Russia sanctions law last month that aimed at clamping down on the Russian oil and gas revenues that fuel its war against Ukraine.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called it "a weak decision, unfortunately, a weak decision by strong partners," according to a statement released by the Ukrainian Embassy in Washington.

Trump announced the deal as his envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner were meeting with Ukrainian officials in Miami to discuss a proposal to end the Russia-Ukraine war.

"I believe our team is simply being used as a smokescreen. And that is certainly not fair. It is certainly not how partners should treat each other," Zelenskyy said.

Trump's move casts doubt on the likelihood of the White House imposing sanctions on Russia this month, given that the bipartisan law passed by Congress directs the administration to target the top importers of Russian oil and gas.

Democratic leaders in the Senate said the decision was tantamount to "selling out Ukraine and our allies in a desperate attempt to save Trump's political prospects," arguing it was Trump's war in Iran that had driven oil and gas prices higher ahead of the Nov. 3 elections.

Trump did not address the sanctions or Russia's war but said, "Lower prices for Americans, especially our Great Farmers, Ranchers, and Truckers, is my Greatest Priority."

Trump said later as he left the White House for a campaign rally that he was thankful for the deal. "I want to thank President Putin. To be honest with you, we have massive amounts of oil coming into our country, and it's diesel, which is what we want. So, thank you," Trump said. He did not answer shouted questions about the criticism from Zelenskyy.

Washington and Moscow offer few details on deal

The White House did not immediately respond to questions about who was paying for the Russian diesel or when it would become available.

Gas prices globally have surged as the war in Iran upends the energy sector. While diesel future prices dipped on the news on Friday, the national average for a gallon of diesel in the U.S. remained high at $6.28, according to AAA, after hitting a record $6.52 on Sept. 22.

A statement from Putin, released by the Kremlin on Friday, said during their call he and Trump dedicated "significant attention to the prospects of resolving the Ukrainian crisis" and also discussed "the situation around Iran and various aspects of bilateral relations."

Russia "confirmed its readiness to supply oil and oil products to the American and global markets," Putin said. "I am confident that this will have a positive impact on the entire global economy."

Russian presidential aide Yuri Ushakov, speaking later to reporters, wouldn't say whether the U.S. made any concessions in exchange for the supplies, or what, if anything, was promised to Russia in exchange.

Trump and Putin's deal draws immediate backlash

Zelenskyy, in a lengthy post online reacting to the deal, said Russia would repay it "with further terror and perfidy." He cast it as an investment in the war, allowing it to be prolonged.

"It plays into Russia's hands — allowing it to kill more, wage war for longer, have even less respect for America, and inflict even greater losses and damage on the world," he said.

Democratic Sen. Richard Blumenthal, who co-sponsored the Russia sanctions law, said Trump's decision "makes us complicit in Putin's war against Ukraine." In his scathing statement, Blumenthal invoked the memory of Sen. Lindsey Graham, a Trump ally and Russia hawk, for whom the law is named.

"This agreement with a murdering dictator is a stain on our nation's character, an insult to Lindsey Graham's memory, and directly contrary to Congress's intent in our bipartisan sanctions bill," he said.

Rep. Don Beyer, the senior House Democrat on the Joint Economic Committee, called Trump's announcement "infuriating."

"This is what we warned anyone who would listen: Trump isn't the slightest bit trustworthy when it comes to Russia," Beyer said in a statement on X.

The law Trump signed last month envisions sanctions on Russian officials, banks and a shadow fleet of tankers and bans all new U.S. investment in Russia and the handling of sovereign debt.

It also directed Trump to impose tariffs of up to 100% on the top five importers of Russian oil or natural gas, with an exception for countries that import less than 15% of Russia's natural gas exports and have taken significant steps to reduce those imports.

The U.S. has not imported Russian oil or gas since 2022, when the Biden administration banned the imports because of Moscow's invasion of Ukraine, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration.

Treasury Department moves to ease diesel sanctions for six months

Shortly after Trump made the announcement, the Treasury Department said it was immediately issuing a temporary license allowing Russian diesel to be supplied to the global market.

This is the latest license the U.S. Treasury has issued regarding Russian fuel shipments since the start of the Iran war early this year. But it is the first to ease sanctions on diesel for a period lasting longer than the standard 30-day window since the start of the Ukraine war in February 2022.

The new so-called general license means U.S. sanctions will not apply until April 2027 on deliveries of Russian diesel that has been loaded onto tankers as of Friday. The department extended similar easing of sanctions in March and April even though Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent had ruled out such a move earlier in the year.

The extensions underscore how the fallout from the Iran war has boosted Moscow's ability to profit from its energy exports.

It's unclear how the move will impact oil prices

"What does this do to prices? I think probably not much," said Clayton Seigle, an energy strategist and expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies.

But, Seigle said the new deal is a "great benefit to Russia and to Putin," who are currently trying to offload their summer-grade diesel for the heavier winter and arctic grades that they will need in the coming months.

"It's kind of shuffling deck chairs on the Titanic," said Michael Lynch of the Energy Policy Research Foundation, a non-partisan research institution focused on energy and economics.

"If we get diesel from Russia, basically it means that their existing customers are not going to get it and they'll have to go somewhere else, and that will keep the price basically where it is now," Lynch said.

Russia, once a major exporter of diesel, has banned exports since July as it has struggled to meet demand inside the country because of Ukraine's repeated attacks on Russian oil refineries. The International Energy Agency says Russian diesel output has fallen by about 30%.

Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak told state news agency Tass that Russia is "immediately starting to lift restrictions on diesel exports ahead of schedule." He said Moscow could start supplies to the U.S. this month and Russia's domestic market will be "fully supplied" with diesel, as well.

Associated Press writers Will Weissert and Konstantin Toropin in Washington, Alex Veiga in Los Angeles and Farnoush Amiri in New York contributed to this report.
